title: Network of GNSS-disciplined clocks: holdover from peers, spoof isolation by cross-node consistency, ADEV-weighted ensemble
summary: A stdlib-only simulation of six GNSS-disciplined sites (TCXO, OCXO, CSAC, Rb oscillators imported from timing-holdover) linked by PTP-like two-way time transfer with static path asymmetry, exponential queueing delay and a lucky-packet filter. Three scenarios: regional jamming where GNSS-less nodes hold time from peers vs alone; a 1-50 ns/s time push on one node caught by a least-squares cross-node consistency check that isolates it before GNSS-denied nodes take its time; and all GNSS lost, comparing every node alone, following the best clock, and an Allan-deviation-weighted paper-clock ensemble. Reports time error per node, time under 1 / 1.5 / 5 / 10 us budgets (G.8271 levels), detection time, false alarms, and how much uncalibrated or changed path asymmetry costs (A/2).
verified: Ran with python3.14.7 stdlib on 2026-11-06, default arguments, 51 s; output pasted verbatim in README (plus a --temp-fraction 0 run of scenario c). 10 unittest tests pass under plain /opt/homebrew/bin/python3 (3.14.7) in about 3 s, including a same-seed check that an added 2 us asymmetry moves time by exactly 1 us, a no-spoof control and a planted blind-detector control. Oscillator parameters are the parent's datasheet/table values; network delays, asymmetries, PPS noise, temperature fraction, site layout and thresholds are stated assumptions. No hardware, PTP logs or real GNSS data; none of the related repos was run.
shows: Six GNSS-disciplined sites over PTP-like links: holdover from peers vs alone under regional jamming, cross-node consistency check isolating a time push, ADEV-weighted ensemble vs best clock, cost of path asymmetry
key_result: [Synthetic network, 10 seeds](README.md#output-ran-on-2026-11-06-python-3147-default-arguments-51-s): jammed TCXO alone exceeds 1.5 us after 16-22 min, from peers stays under 1 us for 24 h; 50 ns/s push on the relay isolated in 50 s (5/5), downstream nodes 332 ns vs 360 us unguarded, 0 false alarms in 40 h; unknown asymmetry A costs A/2 (4 us => 2.16 us); all GNSS lost 24 h worst node: ensemble 1.13 us, best clock 2.27 us, alone 4.18 ms
